research_evidence: عَطِيَّةُ بْنُ عُرْوَةَ السَّعْدِيُّ مِنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ لَهُ صُحْبَةٌ

It lists him as narrating from 'Abdullah bin 'Umar and 'Abdullah bin 'Amr, with students including Qasim bin Rabi'a, 'Ali bin Zayd, and Muhammad bin Sirin. Note: this page classes him in the successor generation, while our dataset lists him among the companions; his companionship is a known point of dispute.

bio: The page identifies 'Alqama bin Nadla bin 'Abd al-Rahman bin 'Alqama al-Kinani, who resided in Mecca. His companionship is disputed: he is mentioned in some sources among the companions but classified by others as belonging to the successors. 'Uthman bin Abi Sulayman al-Makki transmitted from him.

full_name_ar: عمرو بن الحمق ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The page identifies 'Amr bin al-Hamiq bin al-Kahin al-Khuza'i as a companion of the Prophet who fought at Jamal, Siffin and Nahrawan alongside 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. He was killed in 50 AH near Mosul, and his head was reportedly the first to be paraded in the Levant.
research_evidence: قتل سنة 50 هـ

bio: The page identifies Ghurfa bin al-Harith al-Kindi, kunya Abu al-Harith, as a companion who came as part of the Yemen delegation and witnessed the Farewell Pilgrimage. He settled in Egypt. Ka'b bin 'Alqama and 'Abdullah bin al-Harith al-Azdi transmitted from him.

bio: The page identifies Malik bin Hubayra bin Khalid bin Muslim al-Kindi al-Sukuni as having companionship with the Prophet. He resided in Egypt and served as governor of Homs under Mu'awiya, appointed in 56 AH and removed in 57 AH, and died during the time of Marwan ibn al-Hakam. Marthad bin 'Abdullah al-Yazani (Abu al-Khayr) transmitted from him.
research_evidence: كان مالك بن هبيرة إذا صلّى على جنازة، فتقلّل الناس، جزّأهم ثلاثة صفوف

full_name_ar: مخارق بن سليم الشيباني أبو قابوس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The page identifies Mukhariq bin Sulaym al-Shaybani, kunya Abu Qabus, counted among the Kufans. Scholars disagree on his companionship: al-Dhahabi considered him a companion, Ibn Hajar recorded his companionship as disputed, and Ibn Hibban listed him among the successors. He heard 'Ammar on the day of al-Jamal, and his sons Qabus and 'Abdullah narrated from him.
research_evidence: مخارق بن سليم الشيباني، يعد في الكوفيين، سمع عمارا يوم الجمل
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: The Tahdhib al-Kamal entry identifies Abu al-Azhar al-Anmari, also said to be called Abu Zuhayr, as a companion associated with al-Sham who transmitted three hadiths from the Prophet. Khalid bin Ma'dan and Shurayh bin 'Ubayd narrated from him.

bio: The section of al-Mu'jam al-Kabir devoted to Rabi'a bin 'Abbad al-Dili records his report of seeing the Messenger of Allah standing at 'Arafat among the polytheists before Islam and later after his mission. His son narrated from him, transmitted onward through 'Ata' bin al-Sa'ib.

bio: The page identifies Nasr bin 'Asim al-Laythi al-Basri as a successor, jurist and eloquent scholar of Arabic who died in 89 AH (some sources say 90 or 100 AH). He studied under Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, is credited as one of the earliest systematizers of Arabic grammar, and is reported to have been the first to add diacritical dots to Quranic manuscripts. Students include Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' and Qatada bin Di'ama.
notable_works: early diacritical pointing of the Quranic text
research_evidence: كان فقيهاً عالماً بالعربية، فصيحاً

bio: Per tarajm.com, Fatima bint al-Yaman was a female companion (صحابية جليلة), the sister of Hudhayfa bin al-Yaman, whose father's name was Husayl. She narrated the hadith إن من أشد الناس بلاء الأنبياء ثم الذين يلونهم (the most severely tested people are the Prophets, then those nearest them) and a report about women's adornment with gold. Her nephew Abu Ubaydah ibn Hudhayfa narrated from her.
research_evidence: فاطمة بنت اليمان، أخت حذيفة بْن اليمان واليمان اسمه حسيل

bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia identifies him as Amir bin Abi Umayya al-Makhzumi al-Qurashi, brother of Umm Salama. He narrated from Umm Salama (يروي عن أم سلمة), and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from him (روى عنه سعيد بن المسيب). The entry records him in four biographical dictionaries; no death year is given.

full_name_ar: كلدة بن الحنبل ( رضي الله عنه

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=2&Rows=1&SID=2415&head=Sunan Abi Da'ud [Narrated by Kulda bin al-Hanbal كلدة بن الحنبل]

bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia records that Kalada bin al-Hanbal had companionship with the Prophet and was the maternal brother of Safwan bin Umayya (كان كلدة ابن الحنبل أخا صفوان بن أمية لأمه). He narrated the account بعثني صفوان إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلبن وجدايا وضغابيس (Safwan sent me to the Messenger of God with milk, young goats and cucumbers). Amr bin Abdullah bin Safwan transmitted from him.

full: Kharija bin Hudhayfa/Hadhafa b. Ghanm b. 'Amir b. 'Abdullah b. 'Ubaid b. 'Uwaij b. 'Adi b. Ka'b
full_name_ar: خارجة بن حذافة بن غانم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Per tarajm.com, Kharija bin Hudhafa was killed in 40 AH by a Kharijite who mistook him for Amr ibn al-As (فأراد الخارجي قتل عمرو، فقتل خارجة وهو يظنه عمرا). He was described as one of Quraysh's most formidable warriors, said to be worth a thousand horsemen (يعدل بألف فارس), witnessed the conquest of Egypt, and served as judge or chief of police for Amr ibn al-As there. He transmitted a hadith about the Witr prayer from the Prophet.
classif: judge or police chief for Amr ibn al-As in Egypt

full_name_ar: سليمان بن أبي حثمة بن غانم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia records that Sulayman bin Abi Hathama was born during the Prophet's lifetime and emigrated as a young child with his mother, al-Shifa bint Abdullah, who gave the oath of allegiance to the Prophet. Umar appointed him over the market (استعمله عمر على السوق) and assembled the people behind him and Ubayy bin Ka'b to lead the Ramadan (tarawih) prayers (جمع عليه وعلى أبي بن كعب الناس ليصليا بهم في شهر رمضان). No death year is given in the entry.

full: Barra bint Aba Tajra bin Abi Fukayha (Yasar)
full_name_ar: برة بنت أبي تجراة العبدرية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: The Hadith Transmitters Encyclopedia lists Barra bint Abi Tajrah al-Abdariyya as a Meccan companion, an ally of Banu Abd al-Dar. She narrated the hadith of the sa'i: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين انتهى إلى المسعى، قال: اسعوا، فإن الله كتب السعي (the Prophet said: perform the sa'i, for God has prescribed it). Safiyya bint Shayba, Umayra bint Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and Mansur al-Hajabi through his mother narrated from her.
